info.description:
yggvault publishes a read-only package mirror API. The same HTTP routes are
served from web listeners and, when enabled, from the Yggdrasil listener.
Listener context affects generated absolute URLs, cache validators, metrics
labels, and Go module host rewriting.

This specification covers:

- service endpoints such as `/health`, `/info`, and `/metrics`;
- mirror catalog and release metadata;
- deterministic `.zip` and `.tar.gz` source archives;
- Go module proxy endpoints;
- Composer v2 repository metadata;
- Atom feeds and metrics snapshots.

The node also serves this document at `/openapi.json`. That route is handled
outside the generated API handler list.

Brother synchronization is intentionally not modeled here. It uses
`CONNECT /rpc` followed by Go `net/rpc`/gob, not REST. Operators can expose
that channel independently on web and Yggdrasil listeners.

## Mounting

Paths are documented as root-mode paths. When `web.static.dir` is empty,
API, browser, package-manager, generated media, and sitemap routes live at
`/`.

When `web.static.dir` is configured, static files own `/`. Package API,
browser routes, package-manager routes, generated media, and the generated
node sitemap move under `web.routing.prefix`, for example
`/pkg/catalog.json` and `/pkg/sitemap.xml`.

Stable service routes stay at their root paths: `/health`, `/info`,
`/metrics`, and `/openapi.json`. The `/info` response includes
`route_prefix` so clients and brother nodes can discover the mounted prefix.

## Package-manager routes

Package-manager endpoints are published per version after content detection:

- Go proxy routes require a usable `go.mod` candidate. If the module path
  must be rewritten and `overlay.go.rewrite_enabled` is `false`, the Go
  overlay for that version is not published.
- Composer routes come from detected `composer.json` packages after
  package-name collision resolution.
- Universal archives do not depend on Go or Composer detection.

## Caching and ranges

Cacheable responses use strong ETags. Metadata is generated in memory and
cached. Artifact bodies are read from the hot cache on disk and sent with a
fixed `Content-Length`.

Archive routes and Go `.zip` routes support single byte ranges and return
`206 Partial Content` for satisfiable `Range` requests.
info.title: yggvault public API

get.description: Lightweight cross-key snapshot containing each key, latest version, operational status, source classification, and source availability. Release notes and artifact lists are omitted. The body is served from the metadata cache and does not perform a live storage scan. Clients should treat both `application/json` and `text/plain` variants as the same JSON document. Query parameters are rejected.

ETag.description: Strong cache validator for the generated response body.

get.summary: Catalog of all configured mirror keys

get.description: Multi-resolution favicon (16/32/48) generated from the node logo. Pre-rendered at startup and served with a strong content ETag. Query parameters are rejected.

Cache-Control.description: Long-lived cache policy for the constant asset.

ETag.description: Strong cache validator derived from the generated body.

get.description: Atom 1.0 feed built from the cross-key release history. New events come first. The feed includes publish events and archive mutation events; a mutation is a separate entry with an ID that includes the content hash. The number of entries is capped by `web.pages.feed_size`. Query parameters are rejected.

application/atom+xml.example:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<feed xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom">
  <id>https://modules.example.org/feed.xml</id>
  <title>yggvault - new releases</title>
  <updated>2026-04-02T09:00:00Z</updated>
  <link rel="self" href="/feed.xml"/>
  <entry>
    <id>ratatoskr@v1.2.3#blake3-24:ef01</id>
    <title>ratatoskr v1.2.3 - archive updated</title>
    <updated>2026-04-02T09:00:00Z</updated>
    <link href="/ratatoskr/v1.2.3"/>
    <content type="html"><p>Upstream re-released the archive.</p></content>
  </entry>
  <entry>
    <id>ratatoskr@v1.2.3#blake3-24:abcd</id>
    <title>ratatoskr v1.2.3 - released</title>
    <updated>2026-04-01T12:00:00Z</updated>
    <link href="/ratatoskr/v1.2.3"/>
    <content type="html"><h2>Changelog</h2><ul><li>fix</li></ul></content>
  </entry>
</feed>

ETag.description: Strong cache validator for the generated feed body.

get.description: Returns the live node health snapshot for the listener that handled the request. The response is not cached and includes the entry source (`web` or `yggdrasil`), current runtime status, recent diagnostic count, and the last completed rescan timestamp when available.

Cache-Control.description: No-cache policy for live service state.

get.summary: Health status for the current entry channel

get.description: Public node identity shared by all routes: name, optional description, optional location, public contacts, clearnet domain, and Yggdrasil host. The same identity data is also published through mesh `info`/`inet` signals. Empty `domain` or `ygg_host` means the matching entry is disabled.

Cache-Control.description: No-cache policy for live node identity.

get.description: Square transparent PNG of the node logo at a whitelisted edge size (16, 32, 48, 180, 192, 512). Pre-rendered at startup; other sizes return 404. Query parameters are rejected.

parameters.description: Whitelisted logo edge in pixels, for example `192`.
parameters.name: size

Cache-Control.description: Long-lived cache policy for the constant asset.

ETag.description: Strong cache validator derived from the generated body.

get.description: Returns a small HTML page linking the enabled metric groups for the current entry. If both public and internal metric groups are disabled on that entry, the route is not advertised and returns 404.

Cache-Control.description: No-cache policy for the metrics index.

get.description: JSON snapshot of the metadata/hot-file RAM cache and the storage engine (Pebble gauges, event counters, hot-cache enforcement). Served only when public metrics are enabled for the current entry (`metrics.web.public` or `metrics.ygg.public`); otherwise the endpoint returns 404.

JSON snapshot of core HTTP request signals aggregated across operations: request and error totals and request-duration sum/count. Served only when public metrics are enabled for the current entry (`metrics.web.public` or `metrics.ygg.public`); otherwise the endpoint returns 404.

JSON view of the Error Registry: active and dropped diagnostic counts plus the bounded newest-first recent buffer for real-time triage. Served only when public metrics are enabled for the current entry (`metrics.web.public` or `metrics.ygg.public`); otherwise the endpoint returns 404.

Complete Prometheus-compatible text exposition (version 0.0.4) covering every metric group: core, cache, rescan, errors, and internal runtime signals. Built for scrapers such as VictoriaMetrics and Prometheus. Served only when internal metrics are enabled for the current entry (`metrics.web.internal` or `metrics.ygg.internal`); otherwise the endpoint returns 404.

JSON snapshot of the rescan integrator: cycle, publish, and unavailability totals, mean cycle duration, and the last completed rescan timestamp. Served only when public metrics are enabled for the current entry (`metrics.web.public` or `metrics.ygg.public`); otherwise the endpoint returns 404.
Open Graph banner for the whole node (catalog page): mirror-key and version counts, plus the last publish date. Generated on demand and cached. Query parameters are rejected.

ETag.description: Strong cache validator derived from content freshness.

get.description: Open Graph banner for one mirror key: key name, latest version, version count, and last publish date. Unknown or empty keys return 404. Generated on demand and cached. Query parameters are rejected.

ETag.description: Strong cache validator derived from key content freshness.

get.description: Open Graph banner for one version: version string, mirror key, source size, and detected overlays. Unknown key/version pairs return 404. Generated on demand and cached. Query parameters are rejected.

ETag.description: Strong cache validator derived from key content freshness.

get.description: Returns Composer v2 p2 metadata for one package name. `packageFile` contains the package segment with `.json` for stable metadata or `~dev.json` for the dev variant, for example `monolog.json` or `monolog~dev.json`. Unknown package names, dev-only misses, and invalid filenames return 404. Query parameters are rejected.

parameters.description: Composer package metadata filename, for example `monolog.json` or `monolog~dev.json`.
parameters.name: packageFile

200.description: Composer v2 metadata for one package.

Cache-Control.description: Cache policy for generated Composer metadata.

ETag.description: Strong cache validator for the generated p2 document.

get.description: Returns the Composer repository `packages.json` document. yggvault uses the Composer v2 lazy metadata flow: the root document advertises the p2 `metadata-url`, the complete prebuilt package-name list, and the package list endpoint. Query parameters are rejected.

Cache-Control.description: Cache policy for generated Composer metadata.

ETag.description: Strong cache validator for the generated root document.

get.description: Returns available Composer package names after package-name collision resolution. The optional `filter` supports Composer-style `*` wildcards and is validated before matching so oversized or malformed filters return 400.

Cache-Control.description: Cache policy for generated Composer metadata.

ETag.description: Strong cache validator for the generated package list.

get.description: Sitemap of crawlable HTML pages for the current entry: catalog, mirror-key pages, version pages with path-safe version labels, and the metrics index when public metrics are enabled. Absolute URLs use the entry scheme, host, and nested prefix; the URL count is capped by `web.pages.sitemap_size`. Query parameters are rejected.

ETag.description: Strong cache validator derived from the entry host and content freshness.

get.description: Returns the Go proxy `@latest` JSON document for the newest active canonical version in the requested major line. The route is available only when content detection has published a Go overlay for the key and major path.

ETag.description: Strong cache validator for the generated response body.

get.summary: Latest version metadata for the Go module proxy

get.description: Returns the Go proxy `@v/list` body: one canonical version per line, newest first. The route is available only for keys and major lines where content detection has published a Go overlay. Query parameters are rejected.

ETag.description: Strong cache validator for the generated response body.

get.description: Go module proxy endpoint. The file extension selects the body: `.info` returns the Go proxy info JSON, `.mod` returns the raw or rewritten `go.mod`, and `.zip` streams the Go module zip from the hot cache. Versions are unescaped before lookup. The route is available only when content detection has published a Go overlay. If import rewriting is required but `overlay.go.rewrite_enabled` is false, the Go artifact is not published. Composer dist and universal `.tar.gz` archives are served from `/<key>/<version>.{zip,tar.gz}` instead.

parameters.description: Version file name, for example `v1.2.3.info`, `v1.2.3.mod`, or `v1.2.3.zip`.
parameters.name: versionFile

Accept-Ranges.description: Byte range support marker for zip artifacts. The value is `bytes`.

Content-Length.description: Body size in bytes. Zip responses use a fixed length, not chunked transfer.

ETag.description: Strong cache validator for the generated body or zip artifact.

Last-Modified.description: Modification time of the opened hot-cache zip file.

get.description: Returns the latest indexed version for a mirrored key as a newline-terminated plain-text body. Unknown keys or keys without indexed versions return 404.

200.description: Latest version followed by a newline.

ETag.description: Strong cache validator for the generated response body.

get.summary: Latest mirrored version as plain text

get.description: Returns all indexed versions for a mirrored key as a newest-first plain-text list with one version per line. Unknown keys or keys without indexed versions return 404.

200.description: Newest-first plain-text list with one version per line.

ETag.description: Strong cache validator for the generated response body.

get.summary: Mirrored version list as plain text

get.description: Returns all indexed versions for a mirrored key as a newest-first JSON array body. The current handler serves this JSON body as `text/plain`; clients should parse the body content instead of relying on an `application/json` media type.

200.description: Newest-first JSON array of version records with integrity metadata.

ETag.description: Strong cache validator for the generated response body.

get.summary: Mirrored version list with tree hash and source size

get.description: Lightweight release snapshot for one key. Each item contains version, time, size, and a link to the detail document; release notes and artifact lists are intentionally omitted. Pagination uses keyset cursors: `?after=<next-from-previous-response>`. The `next` field is omitted on the last page. Clients should treat both `application/json` and `text/plain` variants as the same JSON document.

ETag.description: Strong cache validator for the generated response body.

get.summary: Paginated release list for one key

get.description: Atom 1.0 feed for release history events of one key. New events come first. The feed includes publish events and archive mutation events; a mutation is a separate entry with an ID that includes the content hash. The number of entries is capped by `web.pages.feed_size`. Query parameters are rejected.

get.description: Dispatches by file extension. `.json` returns the release detail document, `.zip` returns a deterministic zip artifact, and `.tar.gz` returns a deterministic tar.gz artifact. If the version is a Go module that requires import-path rewriting, archive artifacts use the rewritten module tree; otherwise they use the canonical stored source tree. A bare `<version>` without an extension renders the browser HTML version page. Query parameters are rejected.
